title: Apple Is Putting Employees on an AI Budget
content:
Apple is curtailing employee AI use to cut costs, reports Bloomberg. In October, Apple limited some engineers to $200 per day for AI spending, down from $300.
More cuts could be coming, with daily allowances for some engineers dropping to $100. Many groups outside engineering already have a $100 daily limit, but some teams could have their spending capped at $25. Apple is asking some teams to use less expensive models or switch to on-device AI. Employees who need a bigger budget will be able to ask executives for an increase.
Engineers at Apple have the largest budgets because using AI for coding can consume a large number of tokens. Apple lets employees use Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and other models. Some Apple employees told Bloomberg that few were using their full $300 daily limit, so the savings may be small.
Apple has also hired outside productivity consultants for some divisions. Combined with the AI cost cuts, the reviews have fueled worries about possible restructuring.
Apple CEO John Ternus took over on September 1, and he reportedly wants to reduce corporate hierarchy and bloat to accomplish more with fewer people.

report.summary: Apple is tightening employee AI spending limits, pushing some engineers toward cheaper models or on-device AI as new CEO John Ternus targets cost and bloat.
report.background: Enterprise AI use has moved from experimentation to budget scrutiny as token-based pricing makes coding assistants and chat models a visible cost line. Apple lets employees use Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and other models, with engineers receiving the largest allowances because AI-assisted coding can consume many tokens. In October, Apple cut some engineers' daily AI spending limit from $300 to $200, and further reductions may follow. The move comes after John Ternus became CEO on September 1, reportedly with a mandate to reduce corporate hierarchy and bloat. Apple has also hired outside productivity consultants for some divisions, and the combination of AI cost cuts and operational reviews has fueled employee worries about possible restructuring.
key_points: Apple has reduced some engineers' daily AI spending allowance from $300 to $200, with possible cuts to $100. Many non-engineering groups already have a $100 daily limit, and some teams could be capped at $25. Employees who need more can ask executives for an increase.

Engineering has the largest AI budgets because coding with AI can consume large numbers of tokens. Apple allows employees to use Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and other models. Some employees said few people were using the full $300 daily limit, so the actual savings may be modest.

Apple is asking some teams to use less expensive models or switch to on-device AI. That suggests the company is trying to keep AI experimentation going while reducing reliance on costly cloud-hosted model calls.

The AI budget cuts coincide with outside productivity consultants reviewing some divisions. Employees worry the combination could precede restructuring, especially under new CEO John Ternus, who reportedly wants to reduce hierarchy and accomplish more with fewer people.
report.impact: For the AI industry, Apple's move is a high-profile sign that token costs are becoming a real enterprise budgeting issue, not just an experiment. Companies may respond by routing tasks to cheaper or smaller models, pushing more inference on-device, and setting per-team AI budgets. For developers, this raises the value of cost-aware design: token efficiency, model selection, caching, usage observability and fallback to local models. For regular users, the shift could mean more on-device and privacy-friendly AI features, but also possible trade-offs in capability or availability when cloud models are restricted. Apple's scale makes its approach a template other large employers may study.
report.tools: To follow the cost-control trend, watch enterprise AI gateways and observability tools. Open-source LiteLLM can enforce budgets and rate limits across model APIs; Langfuse tracks token usage and costs; Ollama or llama.cpp let you test local and on-device models. Also compare Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini pricing and context limits before choosing a default coding assistant.
